correctness.rationale: Two-way unilateral deviations force exact equality of friend counts across every represented type; the largest-coalition summation forces all types present and equal compositions. Multinomial enumeration proves all counts. The weak-blocker inequalities give lower bounds s, s+1 and neutral/enemy tie-break distinction, and explicit two-type augmentation meets upper bounds. Grand strict-core protection checked. Independent exhaustive finite verifier compares every Nash partition for 102 small type profiles, both preference variants, and all blocking subsets for n<=7; 948546 partitions and 300 blocking minima, but the all-size proof is analytic.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Nash stability here means unilateral entry into another existing coalition (or singleton); core and strict-core blocking correspond to all-strict and all-weak-with-one-strict deviations. Additively separable and fractional hedonic preferences do not define equivalent orderings: a player can prefer a coalition with more friends under lexicographic preferences even when average friend share decreases. General existence is subsumed and explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. The complete all-equilibria partition count and the minimum coalition-cardinality comparison across neutral/enemy semantics are not implied by definitions or general existence.

value.rationale: A complete exact parametric classification for every finite number of social groups is a natural structural solution to the symmetric friend-appreciation coalition-formation problem. The divisor-sum yields all labeled Nash outcomes, while the sharp minimal blocking coalition sizes reveal coalition vulnerability and a nontrivial neutral-vs-enemy separation invisible to Nash stability; neither is a routine existence corollary.
